title: Ang 2–7: Japji on the page
hook: the Japji's pauris fill these pages
tomorrow: where does the morning prayer end and the evening one begin?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang one: the Mool Mantar, without fear and without hate, side by side. Where it begins. Now turn the page.

Weather apps, flight trackers, the little map of a delivery inching closer: a lot of a week goes into watching things nobody can change. So here's an old question in new clothes. How do you live with what you can't control? Turn past ang one and the Japji spreads across the next pages, pauri after pauri, each ending in its own number so you can find your place. And near the start, it answers that question with one word.
screen: `WATCHING WHAT YOU CAN'T CHANGE.` → `PAURI AFTER PAURI, NUMBERED.` → `ONE WORD FOR AN OLD QUESTION.`

segments.voice: The word is hukam: order, command, the way everything is ordered. The first pauri asks how a person becomes true, and answers in the original: hukam rajaaee chalnaa naanak likhiaa naal. Walk in the will of the One, Nanak says; it's written in with you. The second pauri goes further: hukmai andar sabh ko baahar hukam na koe. Everyone is inside the hukam; no one is outside it. Something to tell someone tonight: the Japji's answer to what you can't control isn't to grab harder or to give up. It's to recognize the order you're already inside, and walk in step with it. Now a neighbor who knows this question well. Christians pray the Lord's Prayer, and in the King James Bible it says: "Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven." Shared ground: both put a will greater than ours at the heart of a daily prayer, said by ordinary people on ordinary mornings. And one honest difference. In the Japji, the hukam is already running through everything, with no one outside it, so the work is to see it and walk in it. In the Lord's Prayer, Christians ask for God's will to be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Two old prayers, each in its own words.
screen: `HUKAM: THE ORDER OF THINGS.` · `NO ONE IS OUTSIDE THE HUKAM.` · `THY WILL BE DONE.` · `SHARED GROUND, AND ONE DIFFERENCE.` · then, large: `JAPJI, ON THE PAGE.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write one line by hand, slowly: hukmai andar sabh ko, or in English, everyone is inside the hukam. Let each letter take its time. Then rest your hand on the page and breathe, with one thing you can't control held lightly in mind.
Ang 2. The pages where the Japji's pauris run on, numbered one by one, and where the hukam is named. Today's word.
A line to keep: japji, on the page, where no one stands outside the hukam. Go gently.

howItsDone: Sikhs recite the Japji each morning as part of Nitnem, from memory, a gutka or the Granth; on the page its pauris run from ang 1 to ang 8, each ending in its number.

fork.setup: your little cousin's first big game gets rained out after weeks of practice, and she's crushed. which reply fits the Japji's hukam?

chat.meaning: Both put a will greater than ours at the heart of a daily prayer. The Japji says no one is outside it; the Lord's Prayer asks for it on earth.

notes: 2026-10-15 v3 written: shape wisdom. Question: how do you live with what you can't control? The Japji's answer (hukam, Pauris 1–2), then the unity thread: the Lord's Prayer's 'Thy will be done' (Matthew 6:10, KJV), shared ground (a will greater than ours at the heart of a daily prayer) and one honest difference (the hukam already runs through everything; the Lord's Prayer asks for God's will to be done on earth). Ranking none; not 'the same'. Confirm a Christian reader would find the difference fairly put.

Quoted originals: 'hukam rajaaee chalnaa naanak likhiaa naal' (Pauri 1, Ang 1) and 'hukmai andar sabh ko baahar hukam na koe' (Pauri 2). Confirm transliteration and whether the Pauri 2 line falls on Ang 1 or Ang 2.
'The first pauri asks how a person becomes true' paraphrases 'kiv sachiaaraa hoeeai, kiv koorai tutai paal'. Confirm.
Rajaaee glossed as 'the One who wills' (from raza); some read it as 'the will'. Confirm.
Page detail: the Japji's pauris run from Ang 1 to Ang 8, each ending in its number (numbers were taught on day 1434). Confirm.
Practice rotation: write a line by hand.
